topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students and introduces the importance and scope of studying the complement system.

topics.label: Complement system principles and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental architecture, nomenclature conventions, and central molecular role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three upstream recognition pathways and how they converge to deposit C3b on target surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector functions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the primary mechanisms through which activated complement mediates pathogen elimination and inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the regulatory factors and mechanisms that prevent the complement cascade from destroying host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the distinct clinical presentations and disease phenotypes associated with deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how microbial pathogens evolve specialized strategies to circumvent and survive complement-mediated killing.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
